title: 2016 and 2017 message lengths after omitting F
question: Do both preserved signed messages become prime-length GP rune streams after F is omitted?
summary: Under one declared GP transliteration, the 2016/2017 bodies contain 177/45 runes and four F runes each. Omitting F leaves prime lengths 173/41; omitting W also leaves two prime lengths.

scope.representation: Signed Latin-letter message bodies encoded into GP rune indices by unique shortest aliases with V mapped to U; PGP signature armor excluded.
scope.procedure: Verify preserved message bytes, encode both bodies, count original and F-omitted lengths, then repeat one-symbol omission for each of all 29 GP rune indices.
scope.parameters: 2016 and 2017 manifest body boundaries; fixed GP alphabet; one symbol type removed from each body at a time; primality by trial division.
scope.exclusions: Other transliterations, sentence segmentations, key-layer behavior, unsolved manuscript text or inference of author intent.

finding: The original lengths are 177/45. Each has four F runes, so F removal gives 173/41, both prime. W removal also yields two primes, 173/43; these are the only two of 29 single-symbol omissions with that property under this encoding.
limitations: The signed sources are Latin text, and rune counts depend on a chosen GP encoding and body boundary. The 2-of-29 comparison is conditional and not a probability of intent or an LP2 cipher result.
next_steps: For any proposed LP2 application, fix whether F is copied, deleted or changes key advancement, then predict a full unread passage and compare with controls.

review.reviewer: Deterministic recount of two hash-verified signed bodies and all 29 single-rune omissions
